A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAMMD research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, formatting and appendix organization.

before.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix D report original benchmark experiments, Gaussian simulations, ImageNet and CIFAR10 case studies, error rates and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Wasserstein comparisons, ImageNet null-case results and Gaussian sensitivity analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The NAMMD ratio, empirical estimator, main Gaussian-calibrated DCT threshold, kernel-selection objective, permutation-based TST and NAMMDFuse remain unchanged. The new discussion of a fuller variance calculation does not establish that the implemented calibration changed.

E1.justification: All five original benchmarks and the ImageNet/CIFAR10 applications remain. Appendix E adds controlled Gaussian scenarios, notably estimation-error evaluation with populations in dimensions 2, 200 and 20,000. This extends synthetic coverage without introducing a new application domain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 7 adds an evaluated Wasserstein-distance DCT comparator under the finite-support setting of Table 1. Canonne's test, MMD and the six existing TST comparators retain their roles.

E3.justification: Figures 1 and 6 change the fixed squared MMD from 0.15 to 0.005. New analyses introduce boundary-sampling calibration for bandwidth sensitivity, relative RMSE with 10 samples per distribution, and ImageNet null comparisons at sample sizes 500–2000. The new 150-sample statement in Section 5.2 conflicts with Figure 3's retained sample-size sweeps, so it does not establish a changed ImageNet power protocol.

E4.justification: Existing kernel comparisons and type-I-error plots remain. v3 adds bandwidth sensitivity (Table 14), normalization-estimation-error analysis (Table 15), and ImageNet null-case validation (Tables 9–12), substantially expanding checks of tuning sensitivity, estimation stability and practical calibration.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1.1 newly specifies 300 trials with 300 permutations each for Figure 1, reporting median p-values and interquartile bands. The new analyses disclose 1,000 boundary and alternative repetitions and 300 RMSE repetitions. These disclosures do not establish increased run counts for retained experiments; existing mean±std reporting remains.

E6.justification: All seven v2 tables retain their numerical results under matching content and new numbering. v3 adds Wasserstein results, ImageNet false-positive rates, bandwidth-dependent power and estimator RMSE findings. For example, Table 7 reports blob power at epsilon'=0.1 of 0.968±0.022 for NAMMD versus 0.295±0.047 for Wasserstein. Figures 1 and 6 contain replaced curves under a revised setting, rather than same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1, footnote 6 introduces the condition Var(h1−epsilon*g1)=Var(h1) required for the stated NAMMD variance and describes the full correction using H_ij−epsilon*G_ij. This materially restricts the calibration argument. v3 also adds nondegeneracy assumptions to Lemma 12, explicitly makes Theorem 6 asymptotic, and corrects the MMD inner-product term in Section 2.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction recast MMD's limitation as an empirical finite-sample distinguishability phenomenon, and the introduction explicitly conditions power advantages on the norm condition. These narrow the framing while retaining the central NAMMD/DCT contribution and headline higher-power claim.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly disclaims uniform power dominance, limits the norm/p-value trend to constructed examples, and adds variance-simplification and non-i.i.d. qualifications. It clarifies that accuracy/confidence gaps validate an ordering rather than serve as DCT inputs. Section 2 also newly interprets nonrejection as being 'within tolerance', which overstates what the stated test establishes.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1.1 adds a detailed Figure 1 construction with 30 Gaussian components, 30 dimensions, simplex centres and mixture weights. Section 5.2 newly documents ResNet50 features, deep kernels, median bandwidth selection and grouping 1,000 classes into ten intervals. These substantially improve experimental documentation; the code-access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendix B.4 expand discussion of kernel normalization, continuous similarity testing and optimal transport. Added works include Munk and Czado (1998), Ramdas et al. (2017), and divergence-estimation literature; several earlier density/total-variation citations disappear. The central positioning as kernel DCT for complex data remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the motivation, DCT/TST preliminaries, practical-case explanations and conclusion. It adds appendix navigation and notation sections, moves v2 Appendix A into D.1.2, and separates additional experiments into Appendix E. The title and author list change, and 'margin' becomes 'gap' without changing the corresponding metric definitions.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout with extensive reformatting. Figures 1 and 6 are redrawn with changed scales and captions; notation tables and new experimental tables are added. Retained displays are redistributed, and Figure 4's axis is renamed 'Confidence Gap'.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the motivating example and image evaluations more reproducible, adds useful sensitivity and ImageNet false-positive checks, and qualifies its power claims. These support a limited net improvement in transparency and empirical support. However, the variance condition in Appendix C.1 is neither integrated into Lemma 2 nor established for the experiments, and Section 2 overstates nonrejection as establishing closeness within tolerance.
